images.title: Three guavas, one kilogram
images.purpose: Set up the question: three guavas of about the same size weigh 1 kg together; how heavy is one guava?
images.composition: A row of three guavas on a flat weighing pan at the top, and one long bar directly below, each guava over one part of the bar.
images.exact_structure: Top: one flat weighing pan holding 3 guavas of the same size in a row, filled amber #E69F00. Below: one long horizontal bar for 1 kg, split by 2 grey #6B7280 lines into 3 exactly equal parts, each part plain and lined up under one guava. The left part outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7 with a question label. No fraction written anywhere. Exactly 1 pan, 3 guavas, 1 bar, 3 equal parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any fraction or weight for one guava written in the frame, or bar parts of unequal length
images.takeaway: Share the 1 kg equally among the 3 guavas.
images.description: Three same-size guavas on a weighing pan above a 1 kg bar split into 3 equal parts, one part outlined with ? kg.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the part of the bar under one guava and say what share of 1 kg it is.

image_decisions.why: Lining the guavas up over a 1 kg bar in equal parts gives the method cue without the answer.
